# Pandamonium v1.0.41

Native agents receive Pandamonium context and images while retaining their own configuration. Native history displays photos, and replies return to normal bubbles with compact Worked activity.

## MAD-879 — Agents: add Pandamonium gateway context and bidirectional images

### Problem

Text reached Friday, but the agent lacked the originating interface context and callable Pandamonium capabilities. Uploaded photos did not reach native input, and Desktop history showed filenames instead of images. Friday replies lost their normal bubbles and initially displayed Jarvis's label.

### Implementation

The authenticated MCP gateway projects the existing catalog, extension bridge, tool execution and authority service into native agents. Each turn carries an opaque owner-bound session context. Read-only execution rejects effectful calls; general execution retains both native and Pandamonium approval checks. The setup command adds only the named MCP connection through Codex's native configuration API.

Owner-checked uploads become native images without local-model vision preprocessing. The workstation bridge stages bounded image bytes privately and supports both continuation and active steering. Native history verifies exact task/project membership before reading recorded image references. Final answers reuse existing message bubbles, while visible activity remains collapsed under Worked.

### Product value and UI visibility

Select Friday and an existing task, attach a photo, and send from the normal composer. The selected task and presenter remain attached to the request. Native history shows photo previews that open the existing lightbox. Missing images show an explicit unavailable label. Once its MCP connection is activated, the native agent can discover and use authorized Pandamonium capabilities without moving into the app container.

### Verification

A real Desktop-owned task received and described image shapes and colors while retaining prior context; native history returned identical bytes. A real Codex MCP client discovered and executed the existing runtime-status tool. Regression checks cover owner isolation, authentication, schema and effect validation, bounded image transport, configuration preservation, photo submission to the selected task, optimistic Friday attribution, image previews, lightbox and response bubbles. Full suites and signed artifact verification are recorded in PR #52.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Update Pandamonium and the workstation bridge. Set APP_PUBLIC_URL to the private installation's HTTPS origin so the MCP transport accepts that Host and Origin. Then run the bridge's --configure-gateway command with the /api/agent-gateway/mcp/ URL and refresh MCP connections or restart Codex Desktop once. Existing tasks retain IDs and history. Merely forwarding context does not install callable tools. CT103 installation remains operator-owned; production gateway activation requires that update and configuration.

Native base instructions, tools and configuration remain in effect. The gateway uses the existing private bridge token, expires context after 24 hours or app restart, and rechecks session ownership for each call. Native approval policy can still deny effectful calls. Desktop-owned tasks display native approvals; a headless bridge task requiring approval stops visibly for continuation in Codex. Private workstation history is operator-only, and selected document tools bind the captured document without falling back to another document. Images are limited to 12 and 15 MiB per turn/history page; unavailable source files cannot be reconstructed. Hermes receives compatible image inputs, but live Hermes acceptance has not been verified. No dependency or database schema changes.
